name: Patchwork Runner Low
description: What started as a mass-market athletic shoe has been repaired so many times it's barely the original product. The upper is a mosaic of synth-mesh panels in mismatched colors — grey, faded red, dirty white — each one covering a hole or a split seam. The sole is delaminating at the heel, fixed with a thick bead of structural adhesive that dried yellow.
what_it_says: You've had these shoes for years. You'll have them for a few more. Waste nothing.
worn_by: anyone who grew out of their last pair and couldn't afford new ones
story_hooks: The original shoe's embedded loyalty-chip is still active, pinging a defunct storefront's network — someone might still be listening.
A kid's been wearing the same pair for three years. The day they get new shoes means something changed.
